translationRepairs: Tang put on a show of surprise. "Almost certainly some old enemy of Li Wen," he said.
Tang put on a show of surprise. "Probably one of Wen's old acquaintances with a grudge against him," he said.
文故人怨之 means an old acquaintance of Wen who bore him a grudge; the revision restores both ideas in natural dialogue.
Another attendant forced himself on a palace maidservant; her brother laid a complaint. Anshi said, "The girl is a bondservant venting spite—she slanders a man who wears official cap and gown."
A gentleman-attendant had illicit relations with a palace maid. Her brother lodged a complaint. Anshi said, "The slave is acting out of resentment and falsely smearing an official."
淫 does not establish coercion, and after 婢兄自言 the 奴 Anshi blames is the accusing brother, not the maidservant; the revision keeps those references clear.
He had the girl reassigned as a punishment slave.
He ordered the office to punish the accusing slave.
告署適奴, with 適 read as 謫, has Anshi order the office to punish the accusing slave; the palace maid was already 官婢 and is not reassigned here.
He reported and marked him fit for slave.
He notified the office and had the slave punished.
With 適 read 謫, the literal sense is notifying the office and punishing the slave, not marking someone fit for slave status.
Seeing how exalted he and his father had become, Anshi grew uneasy. He asked that his son Yanshou be given a provincial post, and the emperor appointed Yanshou governor of Beidi.
Seeing how exalted he and his son had become, Anshi grew uneasy. He asked that his son Yanshou be given a provincial post, and the emperor appointed Yanshou governor of Beidi.
安世自見父子尊顯 followed by 為子延壽 identifies the exalted pair as Anshi and his son, not Anshi and his father.
A gentleman violated a palace slave girl; the girl's elder brother spoke for himself; Anshi said, "The slave in resentment and anger falsely defiled cap and robe."
A gentleman-attendant had illicit relations with a palace maid. Her elder brother lodged a complaint. Anshi said, "The slave, out of resentment and anger, falsely smeared an official."
淫 does not establish coercion, 婢兄自言 is the maid's brother lodging the complaint, and 衣冠 denotes an official; the revision corrects all three references.
In Wang Mang's time he did not lose the noble; in the Jianwu years he passed through offices to grand minister of works, again enfeoffing a separate village of Fuping as Marquis of Wushi.

In Wang Mang's time he did not lose his noble title; in the Jianwu years he passed through offices to grand minister of works, and was again enfeoffed with a separate village of Fuping as Marquis of Wushi.

s0191 不失爵 means he did not lose his noble title; bare “the noble” is incomplete. 更封富平之別鄉為武始侯 is a passive re-enfeoffment of the subject as Marquis of Wushi, not him actively enfeoffing; the proposed literal restores both.
